correctness.rationale: For all odd primes and all integer exponents r>=3, endpoint symmetry yields the linear factor and integral monic reciprocal quotient; interior p^r divisibility makes the quotient translated by -1 Eisenstein with exactly p-adic constant valuation one. Newton slopes and derivative valuations give total ramification and discriminant exponent p-2 plus the unit congruence. Laguerre multiplier sequences and separability prove all real negative simple roots and reciprocal counts. Exact standard-library checks replay 12 cases, 78 coefficient checks, 12 Sylvester discriminants and 6 Sturm root counts; finite checks do not constitute the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The assessed new claim is the *combined* prime-index r>=3 classification: factorization into a linear and one rational/local irreducible factor, all-real reciprocal root placement, precise tame p-adic root valuations and discriminant unit. Full accessible primary sources on these very binomial-power sequences address congruences or unweighted recurrence/Apéry limits; Pólya–Schur supplies the classical real-root argument. The r=2 Legendre family is excluded in light of stronger existing work. Exact targeted literature-index and source searches revealed adjacent but non-implicating objects, not a stronger theorem for this indexed polynomial. Residual risk is explicit.
residual_risks: Equivalent coverage in an unlocated paper on Franel polynomials, generalized binomial-polynomial Eisenstein translations or discriminants cannot be excluded.
Literature searching does not certify novelty or give independent peer review.

value.rationale: A natural two-parameter polynomial encoding cubic and higher binomial-power/Franel numbers receives a complete prime-index factorization and sharp local arithmetic classification including discriminant unit, with a simultaneously precise real-root arrangement. Such information is not determined by the classical Franel-number recurrences or values at one; the p-adic extension and discriminant are intrinsic arithmetic invariants. Although the proof uses standard tools, the coordinated classification is nontrivial and mathematically motivated rather than an arbitrary slice.
